results.title: OSP examines alleged irregularities in GH¢49.7m South Africa evacuation expenditure
results.content: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) is examining allegations of corruption and corruption-related offences arising from the government's expenditure of GH¢49.7 million on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa.

results.title: Accra to host maiden Citizens International Masters Hockey tournament
results.content: Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda will battle for honours in the Men’s Over-40, Men’s Over-50 and Women’s Over-35 competitions at the Theodosia Okoh Hockey Stadium in Accra.

results.title: Samuel Ayeh accuses NPP of campaign of vendetta against Foreign Affairs Minister Ablakwa
results.content: A presidential aide, Samuel Ayeh, has accused the New Patriotic Party (NPP) of pursuing a campaign of vendetta and character assassination against Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. He said allegations raised by the NPP’s National Communications Director, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, and members of the Minority Caucus in Parliament were part of a broader effort to discredit the Minister. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse, Mr Ayeh linked the alleged campaign to the Minister’s role in the NPP’s defeat in the 2024 general elections. "This whole agenda and press conference held by my good brother Miracles and the members of the Minority are part of a grand scheme of a campaign of vendetta and character assassination targeted against the Foreign Minister because in their view he was very instrumental in their defeat in 2024," he said.

results.title: TTAG directs unpaid teacher trainees to submit details over allowance delays
results.content: The Teacher Trainees’ Association of Ghana (TTAG) has directed students who have not received any allowance in the first and second disbursements to submit their details to their respective local executives by Tuesday, November 10.

results.title: Ghana Energy Awards announces 2026 shortlisted nominees after record-breaking 600+ submissions
results.content: The Secretariat of the prestigious Ghana Energy Awards (GEA) has officially announced the shortlisted nominees for the 2026 edition of the Awards, marking a significant milestone in the scheme’s 10-year journey of recognising excellence, innovation and outstanding contributions to Ghana’s energy sector.

results.title: Taxing the Unborn: Why Ghana’s best enterprise reforms must reach the tax counter
results.content: On 4 November 2026, the @Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC) published two notices that barely registered above the daily political noise. Exercising its powers under Section 289(5) of the Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992), the Registrar dissolved 323 companies in Companies Bulletin Volume 49. Another 453 entities were placed on a three-month countdown in Volume 48. They joined thousands of silent businesses struck off the corporate roll over the past four years.

results.title: Some OMCs drop fuel prices ahead of November 16 review as competition intensifies
results.content: Under the current regulations governing the pricing of petroleum products, prices are supposed to be reviewed on the 1st and 16th of each month.

results.title: NPP alleges Ablakwa knew of passport scheme before its exposure
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has accused Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa of having prior knowledge of alleged irregularities in the issuance of Ghanaian passports, questioning his claim that he was unaware of the activities within the Ministry. The party’s National Communications Director, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, made the allegation at a press conference on Monday, November 9, 2026, alongside members of the Minority Caucus in Parliament. He questioned how the Minister could establish that no Diplomatic Passports had been implicated in the alleged scheme while maintaining that he had no prior knowledge of the activities. "How did the Minister know that there were no diplomatic passports if he claims he has no knowledge of the scheme? results.title: Let public officers work, we are ready for accountability-Agalga to Minority
results.content: Majority Leader James Agalga has urged the Minority in Parliament to allow public officers to carry out their responsibilities without undue interference, insisting that the government is prepared to account for its actions.

results.title: Fire destroys 20 wooden structures, two containers and church at Agbogba Yellow Container
results.content: A fire outbreak at Agbogba Yellow Container in the Ga East Municipality of the Greater Accra Region has destroyed 20 wooden structures, two metal containers and a church, the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has said.

results.title: IEA backs government’s decision to join BRICS
results.content: In a statement, it said Ghana’s proposed engagement with BRICS is neither a rejection of its traditional international partners nor a departure from its longstanding commitment to constructive international cooperation. “Rather, it reflects a reasonable and necessary recognition that, in a changing world, countries must continually assess their options and build relationships that advance their development objectives. Ghana must not only maintain its existing partnerships, but it must also explore more opportunities that could contribute to economic growth, industrial transformation, and sustainable development”.

results.title: GoldBod, Indian High Commissioner discuss investment opportunities in Ghana’s gold sector
results.content: Ghana and India are exploring opportunities for closer collaboration in the gold industry following a meeting between Indian High Commissioner to Ghana, H.E. Shri Surinder Bhagat, and Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi.

results.title: Sprayers demand 6-month salary arrears as COCOBOD relaunches free fertilizer programme
results.content: The relaunch of the government’s Free Fertilizer and Agro-Input Programme for cocoa farmers was nearly disrupted as some cocoa spraying personnel attempted to stage a protest at the event over their unpaid salaries.

results.title: Ten years of “Mad Over You”: Runtown’s story comes to Spotify in a new Surround Sound film
results.content: Spotify’s Surround Sound concert film with Runtown celebrates a catalogue that continues to find new life with listeners.

results.content: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says the government’s New Economy programme is a four-year plan to transform Ghana’s economic structure. results.title: Majority accuses Akufo-Addo administration of links to service passport irregularities
results.content: The Majority in Parliament has accused the former Akufo-Addo administration of facilitating alleged irregularities in the issuance of Ghanaian Service Passports, claiming the practice dates back to 2023. The allegations follow a disclosure by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that preliminary investigations had established that 10 Service Passports were irregularly issued to individuals who did not qualify for them, following alleged payments to a syndicate. The Ministry said the irregularities dated back to 2023. The Acting Director of Passports, Mahama Yahaya Amantana, and Alhassan Sumani have been interdicted and referred to the Ghana Police Service for further investigations and possible prosecution. results.title: Tano North MCE awards scholarships to 80 tertiary students, secures support for 40 more
results.content: The Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Tano North, Pius Sampson Opoku, in a major boost to human capital development in the area, on Friday awarded educational scholarships to 80 tertiary students pursuing higher education across key academic disciplines, with a primary focus on Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).

results.title: Speaker Bagbin promises journalists online access to Parliament’s records by end of 2026
results.content: The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has promised to introduce an online system to give journalists direct access to parliamentary information by the end of 2026.

results.title: University of Ghana students protest 26% hostel fee increase, demand UGEL system scrapping
results.content: Aggrieved students of the University of Ghana have embarked on a three-day protest against a 26 per cent increase in hostel fees, demanding an immediate reversal of the increment and the abolition of the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL)-managed hostel system, which they accuse of exploiting students and compromising their welfare.

results.title: Ghana Beauty Awards marks 10 Years, pushes for standards and investment
results.content: The Ghana Beauty Awards marked its 10th anniversary last Friday in Accra, calling for the beauty and wellness industry to become a structured, data-driven contributor to Ghana's economy.

results.title: Galamsey resumes along Tano river, airstrip months after flooding submerged Samereboi
results.content: Illegal mining activities have resumed along the Tano River and near the main airstrip at Samereboi in the Western Region, barely four months after devastating floods submerged parts of the town.

results.title: Cash or Christmas gifts? Ghanaians share their festive preferences
results.content: As Christmas approaches, Ghanaians are divided over whether they would prefer receiving money or physical gifts during the festive season. While some say cash gives them the freedom to buy items according to their needs and preferences, others believe physical presents carry sentimental value and serve as lasting reminders of the people who give them. In street interviews, Joyce Brobbey said she would rather receive money because it gives her the flexibility to decide what she needs or wants. “I would rather receive the money because, you know, it actually gives me the freedom and then the flexibility to choose what I genuinely need or want,” she said.

results.title: Gov’t to unveil plan for new economy to create youth jobs – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government is pursuing a new economic direction aimed at creating sustainable employment opportunities for young people, insisting that temporary job programmes cannot provide the long-term livelihood security Ghana's youth need.

results.title: Home for Christmas or staying put? Residents weigh family reunions against travel costs
results.content: With Christmas approaching, many people are beginning to make plans for the festive season. But while some are looking forward to travelling to their hometowns to reunite with family, others are choosing to remain where they live, citing the cost of transportation and the financial demands of celebrating with extended family. For some, Christmas is incomplete without returning home to reconnect with loved ones, catch up with old friends and take part in familiar traditions. For others, the expense of travelling and meeting family obligations makes staying put a more practical option. Ama Serwaah, a trader, says she is determined to travel to her hometown this Christmas after spending three to four years away from her family. results.title: IEA backs Ghana’s BRICS bid, says partnership could open new markets for businesses
results.content: The Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) has welcomed Ghana’s decision to pursue partner-country status in BRICS, describing it as an opportunity to broaden the country’s international economic relationships, attract investment and open up new markets for local businesses.

results.title: Teachers who abuse students’ trust must be identified and punished – Deputy Education Minister
results.content: Deputy Education Minister Clement Abass Apaak has cautioned teachers against engaging in sexual abuse and other forms of misconduct involving students, warning that those found culpable will face disciplinary action.

results.title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
results.content: At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.

results.title: Stop searching for non-existent scandals – Mahama urges journalists
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has urged journalists to exercise restraint in their scrutiny of government, cautioning against media practices he believes could shift attention from national development priorities to controversies that may not warrant public alarm.

results.title: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents, health ministry says
results.content: Three children and one woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
